draft.title: People changing landscapes
card: People change landforms through their activities. Four common ones are mining, farming, building dams and clearing land.
Mining can dig out hills or make deep pits in the ground. Building a dam floods a valley behind a wall and makes a lake.
Clearing land removes trees and plants whose roots hold soil in place. Farming can also leave soil bare, so rain and wind can wash or blow it away.
Natural processes such as river erosion can take thousands of years. People can change a landscape in months or years, so they often change it faster.
draft.remember: Mining, farming, dams and clearing change landforms, often faster than natural processes.

a.q: Why can clearing land make soil easier to wash away?
opts: Roots that held the soil in place are removed
Cleared land always receives more rainfall
Removing plants makes the soil heavier
Clearing land forms a dam across the valley
a.why: Plant roots hold soil together, so once the plants are gone rain can carry the soil away. Clearing does not change how much rain falls.
a.clue: Think about what plant roots do in the soil.

b.q: A council builds a dam across a valley near Bathurst and a lake forms behind it. What does this show about people and landforms?
opts: People can change a landform within a few years
People can only change landforms very slowly
Dams change landforms only through erosion
Dams cannot change the shape of a valley
b.why: A valley was flooded to make a lake in a short time, so people changed the landform quickly. Natural erosion can take thousands of years, so slow change is the wrong idea here.
b.clue: Compare how long the dam took with how long natural erosion takes.

a.best: Roots that held the soil in place are removed

b.best: People can change a landform within a few years

problems.detail: The distractor 'Cleared land always receives more rainfall' uses 'always', which a test-wise student can rule out without knowing the idea. The card uses 'can'.

Two distractors use 'only' ('Dams change landforms only through erosion', 'People can only change landforms very slowly'). The right option is the only one that matches the card's 'can' wording, so a student could pick it by eliminating the absolutes.
